en.name: Fresh wood ear
en.summary: Fresh wood ear is the hydrated black fungus sold as loose, springy ruffles rather than as dried chips. Kept cold and dry it runs about 3–5 days, a figure taken from mushrooms and stretched slightly because wood ear is firmer and less watery. The serious point with this fungus is not shelf life but soaking: fungus left standing warm and wet can develop a toxin that cooking will not destroy.
en.pantry: Do not keep fresh wood ear at room temperature, and in particular do not leave it soaking on the counter. Hong Kong's Centre for Food Safety warns that black fungus left soaking or standing warm can develop bongkrekic acid, which is heat-stable and is not destroyed by cooking. If you are rehydrating dried fungus, do it in the fridge and use it the same day; if fresh fungus has been sitting out wet, throw it away rather than cook it.
en.fridge: Keep fresh wood ear cold and dry in a paper-lined box at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, where it runs about 3–5 days. That range comes from the mushroom entry, extended a little because wood ear holds up better than a soft white mushroom; no agency publishes a keeping time for fresh fungus. Do not seal it wet in a plastic bag — trapped moisture is exactly the condition to avoid here. Rinse it just before cooking, not before storing.
en.freezer: There is no freezer timeline for fresh wood ear and freezing it raw is not worth doing — the gelatinous texture that makes it worth eating turns soft and weepy. If you want wood ear on hand, keep the dried version in the cupboard, which stores for months and rehydrates in the fridge in a few hours. Dried is the form the market has settled on for good reasons.
spoilage: A slimy film on the fronds
A sour, fermented or musty smell
Ruffles gone soft and floppy rather than springy and resilient
Any fungus that has been left soaking or standing warm — discard it regardless of how it looks
tips: Line the storage box with kitchen paper and change it if it dampens.
Rehydrate dried fungus in the fridge, never on a warm counter, and use it the same day.
Never eat wood ear raw; cook it through.
Keep dried wood ear as the everyday staple and buy fresh only when you will cook it within days.

faq.q: How long does fresh wood ear last in the fridge?
faq.a: About 3–5 days cold and dry in a paper-lined box. The figure is adapted from mushrooms; there is no published one for fresh fungus.

faq.q: Is it dangerous to soak black fungus overnight?
faq.a: Soaking warm and long is the hazard. Hong Kong CFS warns that fungus left soaking or standing warm can develop bongkrekic acid, which cooking does not destroy. Soak in the fridge and use it the same day.

faq.q: Can you freeze fresh wood ear?
faq.a: There is no timeline and it is not worth doing. The springy texture goes soft and weepy. Keep dried wood ear instead.

faq.q: Can you eat wood ear raw?
faq.a: No. Cook it through. Raw fungus is not a safe way to eat this ingredient.

zh.name: 新鮮黑木耳
zh.summary: 新鮮黑木耳是已經帶水、一朵朵有彈性的黑色真菌，不是乾燥的木耳片。保持低溫乾燥大約可放 3～5 天，這個數字取自蘑菇並稍微放寬，因為木耳比蘑菇結實、含水量也較低。這種食材真正要注意的不是保存期，而是泡發：長時間在溫暖環境泡著的木耳可能產生一種加熱也破壞不了的毒素。
zh.pantry: 新鮮黑木耳不要放室溫，尤其不要泡在水裡放在檯面上。香港食物安全中心警告，木耳若長時間浸泡或在溫暖環境擱置，可能產生米酵菌酸，這種毒素耐熱、煮過也不會被破壞。泡發乾木耳請放冰箱泡，並在當天用完；新鮮木耳若已經濕著在室溫放過一段時間，請直接丟掉，不要煮來吃。
zh.fridge: 新鮮木耳請低溫乾燥保存：盒底墊廚房紙巾，放在 4 °C 以下，大約 3～5 天。這個範圍來自蘑菇的資料並略為延長，因為木耳比白蘑菇耐放；目前沒有機構為新鮮真菌發表保存天數。不要濕著密封進塑膠袋——把水氣悶住正是這裡最該避免的狀況。下鍋前才沖洗，不要洗過再存放。
zh.freezer: 新鮮木耳沒有冷凍期限，生凍也不值得——它最迷人的那種脆彈膠質口感會變得軟爛出水。想常備木耳，櫥櫃裡放乾木耳才是答案：可以放好幾個月，在冰箱泡幾小時就能復水。市場最後選擇乾貨，是有道理的。
spoilage: 聞起來發酸、有發酵味或霉味
原本脆彈的耳片變得軟塌無力
任何長時間泡著或在溫暖環境擱置過的木耳——不管看起來如何都要丟掉
tips: 保鮮盒底墊廚房紙巾，濕了就換一張。
乾木耳請放冰箱泡發，不要放在溫暖的檯面上，並且當天用完。
木耳不可生食，一定要煮熟。
日常常備乾木耳，新鮮木耳只在幾天內會煮到時才買。

faq.q: 新鮮木耳放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 低溫乾燥、墊紙巾存放大約 3～5 天。這個數字是從蘑菇的資料調整而來，新鮮真菌沒有已發表的期限。

faq.q: 木耳泡一整夜有危險嗎？
faq.a: 危險在於「久泡又溫暖」。香港食安中心警告，長時間浸泡或溫暖擱置的木耳可能產生米酵菌酸，煮沸也無法破壞。請放冰箱泡，並當天用完。
沒有對應期限，也不值得。脆彈的口感會變軟出水，建議改備乾木耳。
不行，一定要煮熟。生食木耳不是安全的吃法。
